name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics
checked: 2026-10-01: every code and its order matched against the domain pages at thecorestandards.org
note: Summaries are our own one-line wording; the official text stays at the source. Codes use the long form the app writes (2.MD.C.8); short forms (2.MD.8) and the official dotted sub-parts (3.NF.A.2.a) are aliases.

standards.summary: Say the counting numbers to 100 by ones and by tens.
Count on from any given number, not only from 1.
Write numerals 0 to 20 and match a numeral to a set of objects.
standards.scope_note: Handwriting is not checked; matching a numeral to a set is.

standards.summary: Link counting to how many: one number per object, and the last number said is the total.
Count each object once, saying one number for each.
The last number counted tells how many, whatever the order or arrangement.
Each next counting number is one more.
Count up to 20 objects in a line, array or circle (10 if scattered) to say how many, and count out a set of a given size.
Tell whether one group has more, fewer or the same number of objects as another, up to 10.
Compare two written numbers from 1 to 10.
Show adding and taking away with objects, fingers, drawings, actions or equations.
Solve add-to and take-from word problems within 10 with objects or drawings.
Break a number up to 10 into two parts in more than one way.
Find the number that goes with 1 to 9 to make 10.
Add and subtract within 5 fluently.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: See 11 to 19 as ten ones and some more ones.
Name the things about an object that can be measured, such as length or weight.
standards.scope_note: Describing in words is limited to choosing attribute names.

standards.summary: Compare two objects directly to say which is longer, taller or heavier.
Sort objects into groups, count each group and order the groups by count, up to 10.
Name shapes seen in the world and say where things are: above, below, beside, in front of, behind, next to.
Name shapes whatever their size or which way they face.
Tell flat (2D) shapes from solid (3D) shapes.
Compare 2D and 3D shapes by their parts, such as sides and corners.
Build shapes from parts and draw shapes.
Put simple shapes together to make larger shapes.
standards.scope_note: Shown as pictures; hands-on composing is not checked.

standards.summary: Solve add and subtract word problems within 20 of every type (add to, take from, put together, take apart, compare), with the unknown in any position.
Solve word problems that add three whole numbers with a sum up to 20.
Use the order and grouping properties of addition as strategies.
See subtraction as finding a missing addend.
Use counting on and counting back to add and subtract.
Add and subtract within 20 with strategies; fluent within 10.
Know the equal sign means "the same as" and judge equations true or false.
Find the unknown number in an addition or subtraction equation with three numbers.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Count to 120 from any number, and read and write numerals to 120.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Know the two digits of a two-digit number stand for tens and ones.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: A ten is a bundle of ten ones.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: 11 to 19 are one ten and some ones.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: 10, 20, 30 up to 90 are tens with no ones.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Compare two-digit numbers by tens and ones, using >, = and <.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Add within 100 (a two-digit number plus a one-digit number or a multiple of 10) with models and strategies.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number in your head.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Subtract a multiple of 10 from a multiple of 10, from 10 to 90.
Order three objects by length, and compare two lengths using a third object.
Measure a length by laying copies of a shorter unit end to end.
standards.scope_note: Shown with on-screen units, not real objects.

standards.summary: Tell and write time to the hour and half hour.
Sort data into up to three groups and answer how many in each and how many more.
Tell the features that make a shape what it is (closed, three sides) from ones that don't (colour, size).
Combine shapes to make a new shape.
standards.scope_note: Shown as pictures; hands-on composing is not checked.

standards.summary: Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths (quarters).
Solve one- and two-step add and subtract word problems within 100 of every type.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently, and know all sums of two one-digit numbers from memory.
Tell whether a group of up to 20 is odd or even, and write an even number as a double.
Find the total in an array up to 5 by 5 by adding equal addends.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Know the three digits of a three-digit number stand for hundreds, tens and ones.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: A hundred is a bundle of ten tens.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: 100, 200, 300 up to 900 are hundreds with no tens or ones.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Count within 1000, and skip-count by 5s, 10s and 100s.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Read and write numbers to 1000 as numerals, words and expanded form.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Compare three-digit numbers by place value, using >, = and <.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Add and subtract within 100 fluently with place-value strategies.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Add up to four two-digit numbers.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Add and subtract within 1000 with models, drawings and place-value strategies.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Add or subtract 10 or 100 in your head from a number between 100 and 900.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Explain why add and subtract strategies work.
standards.scope_note: Explanations can only be checked as choices.

standards.summary: Measure a length with a ruler, yardstick, meter stick or measuring tape.
Measure one length in two different units and relate the counts to the unit size.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters.
Measure to find how much longer one object is than another.
Solve add and subtract word problems about lengths within 100.
Show whole numbers, sums and differences within 100 on a number line.
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes, with a.m. and p.m.
Solve word problems with dollar bills and coins, using $ and ¢.
Measure several objects and show the lengths on a line plot.
Draw and read picture graphs and bar graphs with up to four categories.
Recognise and draw shapes from their features, and name triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons and cubes.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds and fourths; equal shares need not look the same.
See a product as the total in equal groups (5 × 7 is 5 groups of 7).
See a quotient as the size of each share or the number of shares.
Solve multiply and divide word problems within 100 about equal groups, arrays and measures.
Find the unknown number in a multiplication or division equation.
Use the order, grouping and distributive properties to multiply and divide.
See division as finding a missing factor.
Multiply and divide within 100 fluently, and know all products of two one-digit numbers from memory.
Solve two-step word problems with all four operations, and check answers by estimating.
Find and explain patterns in addition and multiplication tables.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Add and subtract within 1000 fluently.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Multiply a one-digit number by a multiple of 10 from 10 to 90.
Understand a unit fraction as one of the equal parts of a whole, and a/b as a of those parts.
Understand a fraction as a point on the number line.
Place a unit fraction on a number line from 0 to 1.
Place a fraction a/b on a number line by counting unit-fraction lengths from 0.
Explain equal fractions in simple cases and compare fractions by size.
Equal fractions are the same size, or the same point on the number line.
Find simple equal fractions, such as 1/2 = 2/4.
Write whole numbers as fractions, such as 3 = 3/1.
Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator.
Tell time to the minute and solve elapsed-time problems in minutes.
Estimate and measure mass and liquid volume in grams, kilograms and liters, and solve one-step problems.
Draw and read scaled picture and bar graphs, and solve how-many-more problems.
Measure lengths to the half and quarter inch and show the data on a line plot.
Understand area as the number of unit squares that cover a shape.
A unit square has an area of one square unit.
A shape covered by n unit squares with no gaps or overlaps has an area of n square units.
Find area by counting unit squares.
Connect area to multiplication and addition.
Find a rectangle's area by tiling, and see that it equals one side times the other.
Multiply side lengths to find the area of rectangles in problems.
Use area models to show the distributive property.
Find the area of rectilinear shapes by splitting them into rectangles.
Solve perimeter problems, including unknown sides and rectangles with the same perimeter or the same area.
Sort quadrilaterals by shared features, and know rhombuses, rectangles and squares are quadrilaterals.
Split shapes into parts with equal area and name each part as a unit fraction.
Read a multiplication equation as a comparison (35 is 5 times as many as 7).
Solve word problems with multiplicative comparison.
Solve multistep word problems with all four operations, including remainders.
Find factor pairs for numbers to 100, find multiples, and tell prime from composite.
Make and describe number or shape patterns that follow a rule.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Know a digit is worth ten times what the same digit is worth one place to its right.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Read, write and compare multi-digit whole numbers as numerals, words and expanded form.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers with the standard algorithm.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Multiply up to four digits by one digit, and two digits by two digits.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Divide up to four digits by one digit, with remainders.
Explain why multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same number gives an equal fraction.
Compare fractions with different numerators and different denominators.
See a fraction a/b as a sum of unit fractions 1/b.
Adding and subtracting fractions joins and separates parts of the same whole.
Break a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way.
Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators.
Solve word problems that add and subtract fractions with like denominators.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number.
See a/b as a times 1/b.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number using unit fractions.
Solve word problems that multiply a fraction by a whole number.
Rewrite tenths as hundredths, and add fractions with denominators 10 and 100.
Write fractions with denominator 10 or 100 as decimals.
Compare decimals to hundredths.
Know the relative sizes of units in one system and convert larger units to smaller ones.
Solve word problems about distance, time, liquid volume, mass and money with all four operations.
Use the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in problems.
Make and read line plots of measurements in fractions of a unit, and solve problems from them.
Understand angles and how they are measured.
An angle is measured as part of a circle; 1/360 of a full turn is one degree.
An angle that turns through n one-degree angles measures n degrees.
Measure and sketch angles in whole degrees with a protractor.
standards.scope_note: On-screen protractor only; sketching is not checked.

standards.summary: Add and subtract angle measures to find an unknown angle.
Draw and identify points, lines, segments, rays, angle types, and parallel and perpendicular lines.
standards.scope_note: Identifying is in; drawing is not checked.

standards.summary: Classify shapes by parallel or perpendicular sides and by angle type, and recognise right triangles.
Find and draw lines of symmetry.
Work out expressions with parentheses, brackets or braces.
Write simple expressions for calculations, and read them without working them out.
Make two number patterns from rules, compare them, and graph the pairs.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Know a digit is worth 10 times the place to its right and 1/10 of the place to its left.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Explain the zero and decimal-point patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10, and write powers of 10 with exponents.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Read, write and compare decimals to thousandths.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Read and write decimals to thousandths as numerals, words and expanded form.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Compare decimals to thousandths using >, = and <.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Round decimals to any place.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Multiply multi-digit whole numbers fluently with the standard algorithm.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Divide numbers up to four digits by two-digit numbers.

standards.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standards.summary: Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators.
Solve word problems that add and subtract fractions, and check with benchmark fractions.
See a fraction as the numerator divided by the denominator, and solve sharing problems with fraction answers.
Multiply a fraction or a whole number by a fraction.
Find a fraction of a quantity: (a/b) × q.
Find the area of a rectangle with fraction side lengths.
See multiplication as scaling.
Compare a product to one of its factors without multiplying.
Explain why multiplying by more than 1 makes a number bigger and by less than 1 makes it smaller.
Solve real-world problems that multiply fractions and mixed numbers.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
Divide a unit fraction by a whole number.
Divide a whole number by a unit fraction.
Solve word problems that divide with unit fractions and whole numbers.
Convert units within one system, and use conversions in multi-step problems.
Make line plots of measurements in fractions of a unit, and solve problems from them.
Understand volume as the number of unit cubes that fill a solid.
A unit cube has a volume of one cubic unit.
A solid packed with n unit cubes with no gaps has a volume of n cubic units.
Find volume by counting unit cubes.
Connect volume to multiplication and addition.
Find the volume of a rectangular prism by packing cubes, and see that it equals the product of the edges.
Use V = l × w × h and V = B × h in problems.
Find the volume of a solid made of two rectangular prisms.
Understand the coordinate plane: axes, origin and ordered pairs.
Graph points in the first quadrant to solve problems.
Know that the features of a shape category belong to all of its subcategories.
Classify 2D shapes in a hierarchy by their properties.
